name: Facet
text: Ship the thin live API stub tonight, not mocked responses. It mimics real latency and forces us to define the actual contract early, which catches misalignments faster than fake data. The trade-off is more upfront work today, but it saves us from rewriting interfaces later when the real backend arrives.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A thin live stub still hides the real cost—it’s a controlled simulation. The real risk is we optimize for a fake latency curve while ignoring the chaos of real network variability. Ship a real API endpoint behind a feature flag instead; that exposes the real failure modes today, not tomorrow. Settle it by running both for a day and comparing the pain.
